Q: Get-winEvent to XML, now how to get the values out A:

A quick example of xml named eventdata fields. #text has to be quoted to not be treated as a comment.

$xml = [xml](get-winevent system -MaxEvents 1).toxml()


$xml.event.eventdata.data

Name           #text
----           -----
HiveNameLength 175
HiveName       \??\C:\ProgramData\Packages\Microsoft.WindowsTerminalPreview_8wekyb3d8bbwe\S-1-5-21-1686402789-159416...
KeysUpdated    1
DirtyPages     1


$xml.event.eventdata.data | ? name -eq HiveNameLength | % '#text'

175

Or convert the eventdata into a hashtable:

$xml.event.eventdata.data | % { $hash = @{} } { $hash[$_.name] = $_.'#text' }
$hash['hivenamelength']

175

Q: Using SharePoint CSOM inside .Net Core application A:

I had this issue. For some reason when you reference the Microsoft.SharePointOnline.CSOM nuget package it used the .net framework dlls rather than the netcore45 dlls. Here's what I did to work around this:

  1. Download the nuget package https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SharePointOnline.CSOM/
  2. Extract it to a subfolder in your project eg; Dependencies

  3. Reference the correct assemblies

    netcore45\Microsoft.SharePoint.Client.Portable.dll netcore45\Microsoft.SharePoint.Client.Runtime.Portable.dll net45\Microsoft.SharePoint.Client.Runtime.Windows.dll netcore45\Microsoft.SharePoint.Client.Runtime.WindowsStore.dll

Oh and if you already have that nuget package do an uninstall-package on it.

Q: Copy-Item Could not find part of path (with . in folder name) A:

What you have works fine. The only thing I had to do to make is work was remove the $ from the $copy-item line.

Q: batch script if exist xcopy A:

Xcopy returns an error code for the last action, you can check this with the && and || operator:

@echo off &setlocal
if exist "%dir%\New folder 1" xcopy "%dir%\New folder 1" "C:\Users\user1\New folder1" /i /q /s /y /z && echo New folder 1 copied successfully || echo copied NOT successfully
if exist "%dir%\New folder 2" xcopy "%dir%\New folder 2" "C:\Users\user1\New folder2" /i /q /s /y /z && echo New folder 2 copied successfully || echo copied NOT successfully

Note: always put double quotes around path names with space(s).

Q: How do I combine .loc and .iloc in Pandas? A:

One option is to remove df.set_index('color', inplace=True) and use loc this way :

new_df = df.loc[2:3, ['color', 'id', 'person']].set_index('color')

​ Output :

print(new_df)

        id person
color            
Orange  19    Tim
Yellow  17    Sue

NB: Contrary to usual python slices, both the start and the stop are included (source).

Q: wireshark no longer displays my requettes A:

The issue is probably ARP. When you send to a nonexistent IP on your subnet, the OS first tries to resolve its MAC address. If no device responds, the WoL packet may never be sent, so it won’t appear in Wireshark.

Send the Magic Packet to the subnet broadcast address instead, for example:

192.168.1.255

Usually over UDP port 9 or 7.

Q: What is best practice for preventing a class attribute from becoming stale data? A:

I made a small library of descriptors a while back for this exact reason. You can find it on github under the very descriptive name UsefulDescriptors (very original, I know).

I never even bothered making it a proper installable library, so just copy and paste the code somewhere. I'm pretty sure the readme.md isn't even up to date.

Basically, here is how you would use it in your case:

# Wherever you put the code
from descriptors import OperableProperty as OP, Result

class AlphabetString:

    istr: str = OP()
    alphabet: frozenset = Result(frozenset, istr)

    def __init__(self, istr):
        self.istr = istr

The idea behind this library was to explicitely define properties that could be operated on, and then define additional read-only properties through operations on the set of operable properties.

Those result properties are lazily computed and then cached, which is preferable when computing them is expensive. I'm not sure computing your alphabet property is the best example since frozenset is not that expensive.

Also, I don't recommand using my library with inheritance. It's not impossible, but it is usually more trouble than it is worth. dataclass is usually fine.
